entities.label: Nintendo
entities.blurb: Nintendo's Virtual Boy misadventure scarred the company so deeply it sat out VR until a cardboard Labo kit two decades later.

entities.label: IBM

milestones.what: Ran dozens of Second Life islands; interop teleport demo with Linden Lab

entities.blurb: The century-old computing giant that briefly made corporate 'virtual worlds strategy' respectable in the Second Life boom.

entities.label: Fujitsu

milestones.what: Fujitsu Habitat launches in Japan under license
WorldsAway brings the Habitat lineage to CompuServe

entities.blurb: The Japanese electronics giant that kept the Habitat bloodline alive across two continents long after Lucasfilm moved on.

entities.label: Sony
entities.blurb: Sony is the only console maker to actually ship VR twice, riding the PlayStation install base where PC rivals had to sell whole rigs.

entities.label: Ivan Sutherland

milestones.what: The Sword of Damocles head-mounted display

entities.blurb: The father of computer graphics sketched 'The Ultimate Display' on paper in 1965 and then hung it from the ceiling in 1968.

entities.label: Evans & Sutherland

milestones.what: Pioneering real-time flight simulators and graphics hardware

entities.blurb: The Utah firm of Evans and Sutherland whose simulators trained pilots — and whose payroll trained the founders of modern computer graphics.

entities.label: Microsoft

milestones.what: Closes $7.5B ZeniMax deal — id Software becomes Microsoft property

entities.blurb: The platform empire that keeps buying its way into virtual worlds — DirectX, Minecraft, HoloLens, AltspaceVR, id Software — with mixed survival rates for the acquired.

entities.label: Apple

milestones.what: App Store opens, later the battleground of Epic v. Apple
Vision Pro ships — Apple enters spatial computing

entities.blurb: Apple waited out a decade of VR wars before entering with the Vision Pro and a vocabulary that pointedly never says 'virtual reality'.

entities.label: Steve Jobs
entities.blurb: Apple's founder whose exile company built the machines Doom was written on — and whose return trip defined the acquisition-as-homecoming.

entities.label: Richard Bartle

milestones.what: Co-creates MUD1 at Essex — the first virtual world

entities.blurb: Co-author of the very first virtual world, whose player taxonomy is still the field's default anthropology.

entities.label: Richard Garriott

milestones.what: Flies to the ISS as a private astronaut

entities.blurb: Lord British himself, who took the avatar from Ultima's mysticism to the first mass-market persistent world.

entities.label: Jim Clark

milestones.what: Founds SGI on his Geometry Engine

entities.blurb: Sutherland's student who built the 3D-graphics industry at SGI, then walked out and lit the fuse of the commercial web.

entities.label: Lucasfilm Games / LucasArts

milestones.what: Habitat beta on Commodore 64 via QuantumLink — the first graphical MMO

entities.blurb: George Lucas's game studio where Morningstar and Farmer invented the graphical avatar world — and the word 'avatar' usage that stuck.

entities.label: Silicon Graphics (SGI)

milestones.what: Backs VRML, spun from its Open Inventor tech
Second bankruptcy; assets to Rackable; brand later to HPE (2016)

entities.blurb: The 3D-graphics temple of the late 20th century whose machines, OpenGL, and alumni seeded nearly every virtual world that followed.

entities.label: Sun Microsystems

milestones.what: Buys VPL Research's VR patent portfolio

entities.blurb: The workstation giant scooped up VPL's foundational VR patents in 1998, a footnote acquisition that ended the first VR era's intellectual estate.

entities.label: Gabe Newell

milestones.what: Leaves 13 years at Microsoft to found Valve

entities.blurb: The Microsoft millionaire who quit to found Valve and ended up owning PC gaming's marketplace.

entities.label: Origin Systems

milestones.what: Ultima Online proves the commercial MMO

entities.blurb: Richard Garriott's studio whose Ultima Online turned persistent multiplayer worlds into an industry.

entities.label: Jaron Lanier
entities.blurb: The dreadlocked VPL founder who named virtual reality, lost the company, and became big tech's in-house humanist critic at Microsoft.

entities.label: VPL Research
entities.blurb: Jaron Lanier's startup was the first company to sell VR hardware, and its patent portfolio outlived it as the field's buried treasure.

entities.label: Chip Morningstar

milestones.what: Leads Habitat, the first graphical MMO

entities.blurb: Habitat's project leader, whose Lucasfilm lessons and capability-security work underlie four decades of virtual-world architecture.

entities.label: NeXT

milestones.what: id Software builds Doom on NeXTSTEP workstations
Acquired by Apple; NeXTSTEP becomes macOS

entities.blurb: Jobs's exile company whose black cubes hosted the creation of Doom and whose OS came home to become macOS.

entities.label: Randy Farmer

milestones.what: WorldsAway continues the Habitat line at Fujitsu

entities.blurb: Habitat's co-creator who kept shipping avatar communities — and the reputation systems they need — for forty years.

entities.label: Epic Games

milestones.what: Fortnite Battle Royale becomes a de facto social world
Epic v. Apple lawsuit opens the app-store wars

entities.blurb: Tim Sweeney's engine company that turned Fortnite wealth into a declared crusade for an open metaverse — and a courtroom war with Apple.

entities.label: id Software

milestones.what: Quake brings true 3D and internet deathmatch
Becomes Microsoft property via ZeniMax deal

entities.blurb: The Texas studio whose engines and alumni set the technical pace for real-time 3D worlds for two decades.

entities.label: John Carmack

milestones.what: Quits Meta, founds Keen for AGI

entities.blurb: The Doom engine legend lent Oculus instant credibility as CTO and spent a decade squeezing latency out of headsets before leaving Meta in frustration.

entities.label: John Romero
entities.blurb: Doom's rock-star designer whose deathmatch instincts made shared virtual space a blood sport.

entities.label: Tim Sweeney
entities.blurb: Epic's founder-for-life who turned Fortnite money into the industry's loudest campaign for an open metaverse.

entities.label: Michael Abrash
entities.blurb: The graphics-optimization legend whose resume — Microsoft, id, Valve, Oculus — traces the entire pipeline from software rasterizers to Reality Labs.

entities.label: Neal Stephenson
entities.blurb: The novelist who named the metaverse in 1992 and has since been hired, twice, to help build it for real.

entities.label: Jensen Huang

milestones.what: Pitches Omniverse and delivers a keynote starring his own digital twin

entities.blurb: NVIDIA's leather-jacketed co-founder who has run the same company since 1993 and now sells the simulation layer under everyone's metaverse.

entities.label: Marc Andreessen

milestones.what: Co-founds a16z, later a major VR/metaverse investor

entities.blurb: The Mosaic wunderkind who co-founded Netscape and later bankrolled the next generation of virtual-world bets from the VC side.

entities.label: NVIDIA

milestones.what: Omniverse pitched as the industrial metaverse platform

entities.blurb: The GPU company that outlived every 90s graphics rival and now sells Omniverse as the simulation substrate for everyone else's metaverse.

entities.label: 3dfx Interactive

milestones.what: assets sold to NVIDIA in bankruptcy

entities.blurb: Ex-SGI engineers who made 3D acceleration a consumer obsession, then flamed out in six spectacular years.

entities.label: Electric Communities

milestones.what: renamed Communities.com after absorbing The Palace

entities.blurb: The Habitat founders' startup whose decentralized-world dream failed commercially but whose E language seeded capability security for decades.

entities.label: Netscape

milestones.what: Explosive IPO ignites the dot-com era

entities.blurb: Jim Clark and Marc Andreessen's browser rocket that made the web mass-market and then was crushed in the browser wars.

entities.label: RealNetworks

milestones.what: Renamed from Progressive Networks; streaming-media heyday

entities.blurb: The streaming pioneer whose CTO chair was Philip Rosedale's day job while he sketched Second Life.

entities.label: Worlds Inc

milestones.what: Sells Active Worlds after mass layoffs
Sues Activision Blizzard over virtual-world patents
Appeals court upholds invalidation of its patents

entities.blurb: The company that launched two founding 3D worlds in one year, then spent its afterlife suing the industry over metaverse patents.

entities.label: blaxxun interactive

milestones.what: renames from Black Sun Interactive — both names lifted from Snow Crash

entities.blurb: The Munich VRML-community company that literally named itself after Snow Crash's Black Sun and died with the first metaverse wave.

entities.label: THE CONSUMER INTERNET
entities.sub: the web arrives in living rooms

entities.label: Raph Koster
entities.blurb: The designer-theorist whose career — UO, Galaxies, Metaplace, Playable Worlds — is one long argument that virtual worlds should be societies.

entities.label: Ion Storm
entities.blurb: The id-alumni studio whose 'design is law' swagger produced both a legendary flop and Deus Ex.

entities.label: OnLive! Technologies

milestones.what: Traveler launches: floating heads with real-time voice and lip-sync
Traveler passes to the DigitalSpace community

entities.blurb: The company whose Traveler put live spatial voice into a shared 3D world in 1996, decades before that was table stakes.

entities.label: Valve

milestones.what: Steam becomes PC gaming's town square
SteamVR and the HTC Vive ship
Valve Index; Half-Life: Alyx follows in 2020

entities.blurb: Valve's research lab gave modern VR its low-persistence displays, Lighthouse tracking, and the SteamVR platform everyone else's headsets plug into.

entities.label: Activeworlds Inc

milestones.what: Circle of Fire buys Active Worlds and rehires its laid-off team
Reverse merger; becomes Activeworlds.com Inc on Nasdaq

entities.blurb: The small operation that bought Active Worlds from Worlds Inc in 1997 and has kept the pioneer world's servers humming ever since.

entities.label: HTC
entities.blurb: The fading phone maker bet its future on the Vive partnership with Valve and briefly owned the high end of VR.

entities.label: Google

milestones.what: Lively, Google's own virtual world, launches in July and dies December 31

entities.blurb: The search giant whose virtual-world ventures — Lively, Cardboard, Daydream — form a tidy graveyard of six-month-to-three-year experiments.

entities.label: Mozilla
entities.blurb: The open-web foundation whose Hubs proved browser-native social VR worked, then handed the keys to its community in 2024.

entities.label: Sony Online Entertainment

milestones.what: Sold to Columbus Nova; renamed Daybreak

entities.blurb: Sony's MMO arm that ran EverQuest and Star Wars Galaxies before being sold off and renamed Daybreak.

entities.label: There Inc

milestones.what: There.com launches the same year as Second Life

entities.blurb: Will Harvey's polished social world that launched alongside Second Life and lost the long game to it.

entities.label: Will Harvey
entities.blurb: The teenage game-dev prodigy who founded There and then IMVU, betting twice that avatars were the future of hanging out.

entities.label: Linden Lab

milestones.what: Second Life opens with user-owned content
Sansar, its VR successor bet (later sold)

entities.blurb: Philip Rosedale's San Francisco lab that turned a haptics experiment into Second Life and has stewarded it for over two decades.

entities.label: Philip Rosedale

milestones.what: Returns to Linden Lab as CTO

entities.blurb: The metaverse's most persistent believer, who built Second Life, tried again with High Fidelity, and came back to Second Life anyway.

entities.label: ZeniMax Media
entities.blurb: The holding company that collected id Software and Bethesda, then delivered them both into Microsoft's empire.

entities.label: Cory Ondrejka

milestones.what: Architect of Second Life's user-owned content model
Joins Facebook, later leads mobile engineering

entities.blurb: Second Life's CTO who argued users should own what they build, then took the Linden diaspora's most direct road into Facebook.

entities.label: Khronos Group

milestones.what: Takes stewardship of OpenGL from SGI's ARB

entities.blurb: The standards consortium that inherited OpenGL and keeps shipping the neutral plumbing — glTF, OpenXR — every metaverse claims to want.

entities.label: Sulake

milestones.what: Habbo Hotel opens in Finland, then goes global

entities.blurb: The Finnish company whose pixel-hotel Habbo gave tens of millions of teenagers their first virtual world.

entities.label: David Baszucki
entities.blurb: The physics-simulation engineer who founded Roblox and grew a kids' construction toy into a listed metaverse company.

entities.label: IMVU

milestones.what: Founded by Will Harvey, Eric Ries and others; avatar chat with a creator economy

entities.blurb: Room-by-room avatar chat with a massive user-generated catalog, and the startup whose pivots gave Eric Ries the Lean Startup gospel.

entities.label: Mark Zuckerberg
entities.blurb: The founder who bet his company's name — literally — on the metaverse being the next platform.

entities.label: Meta (Facebook)

milestones.what: renames itself Meta around the metaverse bet

entities.blurb: The social network that bought Oculus, renamed itself after Stephenson's coinage, and spent more on the metaverse than the entire prior industry combined.

entities.label: Roblox Corporation

milestones.what: Direct listing at ~$40B; 'metaverse' enters the S-1

entities.blurb: The company that got an entire generation building and monetizing virtual worlds before anyone told them it was a metaverse.

entities.label: Unity Technologies
entities.blurb: The Copenhagen startup whose engine democratized 3D development and quietly powers most social VR, VRChat included.

entities.label: Unity

milestones.what: iPhone support sparked the mobile indie wave
runtime-fee pricing revolt and CEO exit

entities.blurb: The Mac-born engine that democratized game development and quietly powers much of social VR.

entities.label: Metaplace (Areae)

milestones.what: Metaplace closes; company sold to Playdom, then Disney

entities.blurb: Raph Koster's try at web-native, user-built virtual worlds — a decade too early for the browser to carry it.

entities.label: Activision Blizzard

milestones.what: Sued by Worlds Inc over virtual-world patents

entities.blurb: The World of Warcraft publisher that beat a virtual-worlds patent troll in court and then sold itself to Microsoft.

entities.label: Mojang

milestones.what: Acquired by Microsoft for $2.5B; Notch departs

entities.blurb: Notch's tiny Swedish studio whose blocky sandbox became the largest build-your-own-world in history.

entities.label: Markus "Notch" Persson

milestones.what: Sells Mojang to Microsoft and walks away

entities.blurb: The indie coder whose block world became the planet's biggest creative space — and who cashed out of it entirely.

entities.label: Magic Leap
entities.blurb: The most-funded startup in AR history raised billions on secrecy and whale demos, nearly collapsed, and reinvented itself as an enterprise vendor.

entities.label: Oculus VR
entities.blurb: Born from a Kickstarter and sold to Facebook for two billion dollars within two years, Oculus dragged VR out of its twenty-year winter before its own name was retired.

entities.label: Palmer Luckey

milestones.what: Pushed out of Facebook; founds Anduril

entities.blurb: The teenager who prototyped Rifts in his parents' garage restarted an industry, was pushed out of Facebook, and pivoted to defense tech with Anduril.

entities.label: High Fidelity, Inc.

milestones.what: Pivots from open metaverse to spatial audio

entities.blurb: Rosedale's post-Second Life attempt at an open decentralized metaverse that pivoted to selling its best organ: spatial audio.

entities.label: James McCrae
entities.blurb: The Toronto graphics researcher who built FireBox, co-founded JanusVR, and still keeps the native client alive as JanusXR.

entities.label: VRChat Inc

milestones.what: Steam early access; user-built worlds explode
Pandemic-era boom makes it VR's social default

entities.blurb: The company whose anything-goes user-built worlds became the de facto social layer of consumer VR.

entities.label: AltspaceVR

milestones.what: near-death shutdown reversed by Microsoft acquisition in October
Microsoft closes it March 10, folding the team into Mesh

entities.blurb: The social-VR pioneer that Microsoft saved in 2017 and then euthanized in 2023 on the way to abandoning consumer metaverse plans.

entities.label: OpenAI
entities.blurb: The AI lab whose Microsoft alliance redirected big-tech ambition from the metaverse to generative AI almost overnight.

entities.label: Playable Worlds

milestones.what: Reveals Stars Reach, a cloud-native simulated-world MMO

entities.blurb: Koster's latest company, rebuilding the living-world MMO on cloud simulation lessons from Ultima Online onward.

entities.label: Keen Technologies
entities.blurb: John Carmack's post-Meta startup, betting that the man who optimized virtual worlds can optimize his way to AGI.

entities.label: Lamina1

milestones.what: Stephenson co-founds a blockchain base layer for the open metaverse

entities.blurb: Neal Stephenson's own attempt to build the metaverse infrastructure his 1992 novel accidentally specified.
